[Intro: dark drone fades in, galloping toms, breathy sampled hook]

[Verse 1: breathy voice over toms and drone]
You say it doesn't hurt you
I say it doesn't show
We stand in the same kitchen
In two kinds of snow

[Pre-Chorus: plucked string synth figures]
There's a door between us nobody built
I'd open it with anything

[Chorus: soaring, keening, sampled hook underneath]

[Verse 2: breathy voice over toms and drone]
You were raised on different thunder
I was raised on different rain
We learned two words for mercy
And no word for the pain

[Pre-Chorus: plucked string synth figures]

producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 106 BPM, 4/4, B-flat minor, over a drone that barely changes. Relentless, galloping and ritual, like running in a dream.

VOICE: Female mezzo-soprano with a theatrical, wide-ranging delivery: breathy and close in the verses, swooping up into a strong, keening head voice on the chorus. Layered whispered doubles. In the bridge and outro a pitch-shifted low version of her own voice answers her, as if the other person has borrowed it.

INSTRUMENTS: A driving, galloping drum pattern played on deep toms and a dry electronic kick, with no cymbals at all (the engine). A breathy sampled-instrument hook, half cello and half human sigh, playing a short falling phrase (the earworm). A dark, sustained synth drone. Plucked string-like synth figures. A distant, heavily delayed electric guitar that only growls in the choruses. Deep sub-bass pedal note.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, drone fades in, the galloping toms start at 0:05, the sampled hook enters at 0:14. 0:32 Verse 1, voice over drums and drone only. 0:50 Pre-chorus, plucked figures appear. 1:04 Chorus 1, hook returns under the vocal, guitar growl. 1:40 Verse 2. 1:58 Pre-chorus. 2:12 Chorus 2. 2:48 Bridge, chanted on one note with stacked voices, the low pitch-shifted voice joins. 3:06 Breakdown, drums thin to kick alone, the wordless call and the 'raining' question. 3:24 Final chorus, full intensity with the two voices trading lines. 3:58 Outro, the toms keep running while everything else fades, ending on the drone at 4:20.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Dark, wide and immersive. Drums dry and centred, vocals swimming in long reverb and delay, the hook slightly lo-fi and grainy like an early digital sampler.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first entry of the sampled sigh-cello hook over the galloping toms. It should raise the hair on your arms.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: Cinema-grade sub-bass under the drone, and real rain and far-off thunder mixed almost subliminally beneath the breakdown.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Distance, pleading, then communion.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

Two people stand in the same kitchen in two different kinds of snow. One asks the other to trade inner weather for a day, so that nobody has to shout to be understood.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: a marriage trying to hear itself; a parent and a teenager; a friend reaching someone who is depressed or grieving; two sides of a divided family or country; or a conversation with your younger self. 'I'll wear yours out' means both 'I'll wear it outside' and 'I'll carry it until it's used up'.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: an impossible swap as the central idea, a bodily metaphor for emotional work, direct questions to 'you', and a chanted bridge. The opening image ('the same kitchen, in two kinds of snow') is the line people will quote. Designed mishearing: 'Wear my weather' is heard as 'Where, my wanderer' and 'Whether, my weather', each of which opens a different story.
